questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The following are natural resources except
questions.explanation: Cellophane is a synthetic manufactured material, not a natural resource.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All these are examples of fold mountains except
questions.explanation: The Vosges Mountains are an example of block mountains (horsts), not fold mountains.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All the following are fertile plains except
questions.explanation: Erosional plains are formed by the wearing away of topsoil and rock, leaving thin, less fertile soils.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The world population in 2015 was estimated at about
questions.explanation: The world population is approximately 7.3 billion.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Soil factors in an ecosystem are referred to as
questions.explanation: Soil factors in an ecosystem are known as edaphic factors.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: West Africa is located between latitudes _____ and _____ of the Equator.
questions.explanation: West Africa lies approximately between latitudes 4°N and 20°N north of the Equator.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All the following crops are grown in plantation agriculture in West Africa except
questions.explanation: Wheat is a temperate/irrigated cereal grain crop rather than a tropical tree plantation crop.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: In a food chain, the position occupied by an organism is called
questions.explanation: A trophic level is the specific feeding position occupied by an organism in a food chain.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Tropical rainforests can be conserved by the following practices except
questions.explanation: Deforestation is the indiscriminate felling of trees, which destroys rather than conserves tropical rainforests.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Population growth rate may be defined as the

options.text: mortality rate per unit area over a period
number of times an organism occurs within a given period
number of a particular species per unit area
net rate of change in population over a given period

questions.explanation: Population growth rate measures the net rate of change in population size over a given period of time.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Tall trees with buttress roots are associated with
questions.explanation: Tall emergent trees supported by heavy buttress roots are characteristic of the tropical rainforest.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following resources is non-renewable?
questions.explanation: Mineral resources are finite and non-renewable on human timescales, unlike biological resources.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The classical solar system comprises the Sun and its
questions.explanation: The solar system consists of the Sun and eight major planets (or nine in older traditional classifications including Pluto).

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: On September 23rd, towns and cities in the northern hemisphere experience

options.text: equal length of day and night

questions.explanation: September 23rd is the autumnal equinox, when all places on Earth experience 12 hours of daylight and 12 hours of night.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Density, mortality and birth rate are factors that affect
questions.explanation: Population size and structure are directly governed by birth rate, mortality rate, migration, and density.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The predominant system of agriculture among traditional rural farmers in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: Bush fallowing (rotational cultivation allowing fallow periods to restore soil fertility) is the most widespread traditional farming system in rural Nigeria.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: What type of mountain is associated with synclines and anticlines?
questions.explanation: Fold mountains are formed by compressional forces that bend rock strata into upfolds (anticlines) and downfolds (synclines).

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The instrument used for recording the vibrations of an earthquake is called a
questions.explanation: A seismograph detects and records the seismic waves produced by earthquakes.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All of these are major traditional industrial zones in Nigeria except
questions.explanation: Nigeria's four major industrial zones are the Western (Lagos-Ibadan), South-East (Onitsha-Nnewi-Aba-Port Harcourt), North-Central (Kano-Kaduna-Jos), and Mid-West (Benin-Sapele-Warri) zones.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Lines of longitude can best be described as

options.text: imaginary lines on the Earth's surface joining the North and South Poles
the linear distance of a place east or west of the Equator
the angular distance of a place north or south of the Equator

questions.explanation: Meridians of longitude are imaginary semi-great circles running from the North Pole to the South Pole.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The largest planet in the solar system, marked by alternating light and dark bands, is
questions.explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system and features prominent alternating light and dark cloud bands.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the largest and longest river in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: River Niger is the longest and largest river in Nigeria and West Africa, rising in the Fouta Djallon highlands of Guinea.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All these are methods of representing relief on maps except
questions.explanation: A dot map is a statistical map used to show distribution of population or commodities, not topographic relief.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is the longest river in West Africa?
questions.explanation: River Niger (~4,180 km) is the longest river in West Africa.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is not a way of conserving natural resources?
questions.explanation: Poaching is the illegal hunting of wildlife, which depletes rather than conserves natural resources.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The downslope movement of weathered rock materials under the direct force of gravity is called
questions.explanation: Mass movement (or mass wasting) is the movement of weathered regolith down a slope under gravity.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: A horizontal intrusion of magma along a bedding plane of sedimentary rocks is called a
questions.explanation: A sill is a tabular sheet intrusion of magma solidified parallel to the bedding planes of enclosing rock strata.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: In the northern hemisphere, the autumnal equinox occurs on
questions.explanation: The September equinox occurs around 22–23 September each year.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The natural satellite of the Earth is
questions.explanation: The Moon is the Earth's only natural satellite.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The following are direct environmental effects of overgrazing except

options.text: soil and wind erosion of pasture land

questions.explanation: Overgrazing strips vegetation cover, depletes fodder species, and exposes soil to erosion.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Sharp, slender, downward-growing calcite pinnacles hanging from the roof of a limestone cave are called
questions.explanation: Stalactites hang downward from the ceiling of karst caves, whereas stalagmites grow upward from the floor.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following West African countries is landlocked?
questions.explanation: Burkina Faso is completely surrounded by land and has no coastline.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The most important cash crop cultivated in the irrigated Nile Basin is
questions.explanation: Long-staple cotton is the premier cash crop produced under perennial irrigation in the Nile Valley and Delta.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The average density of the continental crust (sial) is approximately
questions.explanation: Sial (silica and aluminium) forms the upper continental crust and has an average density of about 2.7 g/cm³.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The angular distance of a point on the Earth's surface north or south of the Equator, measured in degrees from the centre of the Earth, is known as
questions.explanation: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the Equator measured in degrees.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Hot desert conditions in West Africa are found in
questions.explanation: Northern Mali extends deep into the Sahara Desert.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All of these are elements of weather and climate except
questions.explanation: Altitude is a factor that modifies climate, whereas temperature, rainfall, and sunshine are elements of weather and climate.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a major reason for high population density?
questions.explanation: Fertile soils support intensive agriculture and attract dense human settlement.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: A given map with an original scale of 1 : 150,000 is enlarged 3 times its original size. What will be the new scale?
questions.explanation: Enlarging a map 3 times divides the denominator of the representative fraction by 3: 150,000 / 3 = 1 : 50,000.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is not a biotic factor in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure is a physical (abiotic) factor, while parasites, predators, and grazers are living (biotic) factors.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Water pollution is caused by all the following except
questions.explanation: Oil spills, sewage, and industrial effluents pollute water bodies, whereas rainwater harvesting collects clean precipitation.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence in which denudation occurs?
questions.explanation: Denudation proceeds from weathering (breakdown in situ) to erosion/transportation, and finally deposition.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Because of its oblate shape, the Earth is best described as a
questions.explanation: The Earth is flattened at the poles and bulges at the Equator, a unique Earth-shape termed a geoid.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The following are abiotic components of an ecosystem except
questions.explanation: Bacteria are living microorganisms (biotic decomposer component), whereas topography, water, and wind are abiotic.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following human activities has a beneficial effect on soil conservation?
questions.explanation: Strip cultivation checks surface runoff and soil erosion, helping conserve soil fertility.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The degree of saltiness or concentration of dissolved salts in oceans and seas is referred to as
questions.explanation: Salinity measures the concentration of dissolved salts in seawater, usually expressed in parts per thousand (‰).

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Stratified rocks are also known as
questions.explanation: Sedimentary rocks are deposited in distinct layers (strata) separated by bedding planes, so they are called stratified rocks.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following physical properties is used directly in classifying soil into sand, clay and loam?
questions.explanation: Soil texture refers to the relative proportions of sand, silt, and clay particles in a soil.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The zone of the Earth where life activities take place is referred to as the
questions.explanation: The biosphere encompasses all parts of the Earth's crust, waters, and atmosphere that support living organisms.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Nigeria is located in which subregion of Africa?
questions.explanation: Nigeria is one of the 16 countries located in the West African subregion.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The mode of transport that is most sensitive to poor visibility and adverse weather conditions is
questions.explanation: Air transport is heavily affected by fog, thunderstorms, cloud cover, and crosswinds.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: A great circle can best be described as

options.text: any circle whose plane passes through the centre of the globe, dividing it into two equal hemispheres

questions.explanation: A great circle is any circle on the Earth's surface whose plane passes through the centre of the Earth, bisecting it into two equal halves and tracing the shortest distance between two points.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The catastrophic Bam earthquake that killed about 30,000 people occurred in the year
questions.explanation: The devastating Bam earthquake occurred in December 2003.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The longitudinal extent of Nigeria (from approximately 3°E to 15°E) is about
questions.explanation: Nigeria extends from about longitude 3°E to 15°E, giving a longitudinal span of 15° - 3° = 12°.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The liquid water portion of the Earth's surface is called the
questions.explanation: The hydrosphere comprises all liquid and frozen surface waters (oceans, seas, lakes, rivers) on Earth.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: In which of the following African countries is Mediterranean fruit farming least important?
questions.explanation: Morocco, Algeria, and northern Egypt border the Mediterranean Sea and practice Mediterranean orchard farming, whereas Uganda has an equatorial plateau climate.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The ship canal that connects the Atlantic Ocean directly to the Pacific Ocean across Central America is the
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal links the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans across the Isthmus of Panama.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The most urbanized geopolitical zone of Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: South-West Nigeria (including Lagos, Ibadan, Abeokuta, Akure, Osogbo, and Ilorin corridor) has the highest concentration of large urban centres.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All these are typical characteristics of Nigerian rivers except

options.text: seasonal fluctuation in volume and flooding
shallowness and siltation in the dry season
year-round uniform volume without seasonal change

questions.explanation: Nigerian rivers experience marked seasonal variations in volume between the wet and dry seasons.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All the following are forms of smallholder farming in West Africa except
questions.explanation: Plantation agriculture is a large-scale commercial monoculture system, not a smallholder subsistence practice.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Plants specially adapted to survive in dry desert environments are called
questions.explanation: Xerophytes possess adaptations such as thick cuticles, sunken stomata, and deep roots to withstand prolonged drought.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Very low annual rainfall, sparse vegetation, high daytime temperatures and cold nights are characteristics of a
questions.explanation: Hot deserts receive less than 250 mm of annual rainfall, have sparse xerophytic vegetation, and experience wide diurnal temperature ranges.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following is a type of rapid mass movement (mass wasting)?
questions.explanation: Landslides are rapid downslope movements of rock debris and soil under gravity.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The method used in extracting crude petroleum oil from underground reservoirs is
questions.explanation: Crude oil is extracted by sinking wells with a drilling rig into oil-bearing sedimentary rock strata.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used for measuring rainfall?
questions.explanation: A rain gauge collects and measures liquid precipitation in millimetres.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Natural factors that directly determine the type of climax vegetation in a habitat include all the following except
questions.explanation: Climatic and edaphic factors determine natural vegetation, whereas farming is an anthropogenic interference.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: On a topographical map, water features such as rivers, streams and lakes are collectively referred to as
questions.explanation: Drainage refers to the network of surface water bodies (rivers, streams, lakes, swamps) in an area.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All the following are important timber-producing countries in West Africa except
questions.explanation: Mauritania is predominantly desert (Sahara/Sahel) and lacks tropical rainforest timber resources.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All of these are features of the lower course (old stage) of a river except
questions.explanation: A deep V-shaped valley is a feature of the upper (youthful) course of a river where vertical corrasion dominates.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The point within the Earth's crust where earthquake seismic waves originate is called the
questions.explanation: The focus (or hypocentre) is the subterranean point of origin of an earthquake, while the point directly above it on the surface is the epicentre.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: A natural spring is an outlet on the Earth's surface for
questions.explanation: A spring forms where the water table intersects the ground surface, allowing underground water to flow out naturally.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Loam is the best type of soil for crop production because it

options.text: has a very high percentage of clay that prevents water percolation
contains balanced proportions of sand, silt, clay and humus with good water retention and aeration
consists purely of coarse sand grains

questions.explanation: Loamy soil combines adequate drainage and aeration with high humus content and nutrient retention.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following planets has no natural satellite (moon)?
questions.explanation: Mercury and Venus are the only two planets in the solar system with no natural moons.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: When it is 9:00 a.m. in Munich, Germany (longitude 11°E), what is the local time at longitude 96°E?
questions.explanation: Longitude difference = 96°E - 11°E = 85°. Time difference = 85° / 15° per hour = 5 hours 40 minutes ahead. 9:00 a.m. + 5 hr 40 min = 2:40 p.m.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following statements is not true about the solar system?

options.text: Rays from the Sun provide energy to the system
All planets have the exact same period of revolution
The planets revolve around the Sun in elliptical orbits
The Sun is at the centre of the solar system

questions.explanation: Each planet revolves around the Sun at a different distance and has its own distinct orbital period.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: The spinning movement of the Earth from west to east on its axis once every 24 hours is known as
questions.explanation: The Earth's daily spin on its axis from west to east is called rotation and causes day and night.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: Which of the following instruments is used to measure wind speed?
questions.explanation: A cup anemometer measures wind speed, while a wind vane indicates wind direction.

questions.subject: geography
questions.question: All these are examples of urban settlements except a
questions.explanation: A village is a rural settlement, whereas towns, cities, conurbations, and megalopolises are urban settlements.
